runsOn takes a fractional delay as Node does, truncated, so a 1.9 ms timer stays one of the body's own jobs (rich-unfiled-791c.ffob)

The runsOn descriptions — programTimers' header, the settled message, the
first test's name — now state the rule as it is: a timer still set, or a
longer one fired since the body returned.

runsOn counts a program timer that fires before its 1 ms check, so a stalled loop no longer hides a timer left set (rich-unfiled-791c.ffob)

The 1 ms check is armed as the body returns, and any program timer over
1 ms that fires after that has run on past the body, whether or not the
check has fired yet. Timers of 1 ms remain the body's queued jobs, since
same-delay timers fire in the order they were set.

Markdown reads link reference definitions and resolves reference links against them, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.1dvo) (#441)

* Markdown reads link reference definitions and resolves reference links against them, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.1dvo)

A definition is a block-pass mark the inline pass collects, first label wins,
and full, collapsed and shortcut links and images resolve against it, with the
link rule's fallback from a refused inline form. Containers now take lazy
lines as markdown-it's do and end where their own block pass stops, replacing
the speculative open-paragraph check, so a definition can take a lazy title.

* Markdown reads a container's lines as its block pass reaches them, so a run of quotes reads in linear time (rich-unfiled-791c.1dvo)

A quote copied every line it might take before reading any, so a run of
quotes each followed by a lazy line it did not take read the rest of the
document once per quote: 8 s for 32 KB. Containers now read through Lines,
made on demand from their parent's, and a definition's continuation shares
the one has-text-opens-no-block predicate a lazy line does.

* Markdown reads a definition's destination in the text markdown-it holds for it, ending with its own line (rich-unfiled-791c.1dvo)

A backslash escaping the destination's line ending took the destination on
into the lines read ahead, or left the definition unended, where markdown-it
ends the definition there: "[a]: x\\\ny" defines x%5C and leaves y a paragraph.
